flagships.title: World of Nads
flagships.subtitle: Browser-Based 3D Multiplayer Arena Game
flagships.description: A browser-based 3D multiplayer arena game built with Godot, exported to WebAssembly for zero-install client delivery, paired with a custom Rust-based WebSocket multiplayer server handling authoritative state synchronization, and Monad-focused EVM on-chain prize distribution.

caseStudy.problem: Delivering an uncompromised 3D multiplayer game directly inside the browser without requiring external game launchers or extensions, while keeping player states synchronized in real time alongside wallet authentication and on-chain payouts.
caseStudy.difficulty: Maintaining low perceived latency across client network fluctuations while bridging three distinct execution environments: the Godot WebAssembly client runtime, the browser DOM/JavaScript wallet interface, and a custom asynchronous Rust WebSocket server.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Independently developed the game client in Godot, 3D asset pipeline, client-side movement interpolation, the Rust WebSocket multiplayer server, and the Monad smart contract payout integration.

components.name: Godot Client (WASM)
components.desc: WebGL/WASM canvas managing 3D graphics, local physics simulation, and player input capture.

components.name: JS Interop Layer
components.desc: Lightweight boundary bridging wallet signing and WebSocket packet dispatch without DOM overhead.

components.name: Rust Server Engine
components.desc: Authoritative state synchronization loop, spatial validation, and client connection management.

components.name: Monad Settlement
components.desc: Smart contracts executing deterministic match entry escrow and verifiable prize disbursement.

tradeoffs: Client-side prediction vs authoritative validation: responsive client motion for local control, with server authority during collision and damage resolution.
Custom binary framing vs JSON: eliminated serialization overhead to keep packet sizes compact over WebSockets.
caseStudy.hardestBug: During early testing, browser frame rates plummeted from 60 FPS to under 12 FPS on lower-spec machines. Profiling showed that per-frame interop calls crossing the Godot-WASM to JavaScript boundary caused severe browser garbage collector stalls. Resolved by decoupling rendering from network updates and batching bridge calls into timed intervals with typed arrays.
caseStudy.currentStatus: Playable in modern desktop browsers at worldofnads.xyz. Monad-focused EVM architecture with no Solana dependencies.
caseStudy.nextSteps: Implement client-side rollback lag compensation buffers and optimize initial WASM bundle size.

flagships.title: EEG Communication Headset
flagships.subtitle: Wearable Assistive Interface Concept for Non-Speaking Users
flagships.description: An experimental hardware and firmware investigation exploring an affordable, wearable communication-support interface for non-speaking users. Integrates scalp dry electrodes, a TGAM EEG frontend, an ESP32 microcontroller, audio amplification, and bone-conduction transducers.

caseStudy.problem: Commercial assistive brain-computer and speech interfaces cost thousands of dollars, require messy conductive gels, or depend on continuous desktop tethering, placing them out of reach for everyday mobility.
caseStudy.difficulty: Physiological signals acquired at the scalp are in the microvolt range (10-100 μV) and are easily corrupted by blinks, jaw clenches (EMG), and 50Hz environmental powerline noise. Producing reliable, intentional user triggers on an embedded microcontroller without false alarms requires disciplined signal acquisition and task isolation.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Designed the circuit schematic and breadboard layout, implemented dual-core FreeRTOS firmware in C++ on the ESP32, developed the ThinkGear UART serial packet decoder with checksum validation, and configured the audio amplification circuit driving bone-conduction transducers.

components.name: Scalp Dry Electrodes
components.desc: Single-point Fp1 forehead dry electrode with earlobe ground and reference clips.

components.name: TGAM Biosensing Frontend
components.desc: Hardware pre-amplifier, 50Hz notch filter, and 12-bit ADC outputting ThinkGear packets over UART.

components.name: ESP32 Firmware Layer
components.desc: Core 0 consumes 57,600 baud serial stream; Core 1 evaluates intentional threshold events.

components.name: Audio & Bone Conduction
components.desc: DAC tone generation into PAM8403 amplifier driving a bone-conduction transducer against temporal bone.

auditStatus.componentsAcquired: NeuroSky TGAM module, ESP32-WROOM-32 dev board, PAM8403 audio amplifier, 8Ω bone-conduction transducers, lithium charging regulation circuit.
auditStatus.hardwareAssembled: Benchtop breadboard and perfboard test bench established for signal validation, serial telemetry, and audio triggering.
auditStatus.firmwareImplemented: UART packet parser validating 0xAA 0xAA sync bytes and packet checksums; extraction of Signal Quality, Attention, and raw wave packets; threshold-based event detection.
auditStatus.testedResults: Verified packet integrity at 57,600 baud without buffer overruns on continuous test runs; confirmed audible feedback delivered via bone conduction.
auditStatus.honestLimitations: Does NOT decode continuous speech, arbitrary thoughts, or complex linguistic sentences. The system operates strictly as an intentional state/event trigger mapped to discrete assistive audio cues.

caseStudy.currentStatus: Bench prototype assembled and tested. Firmware signal parser operational. Headband ergonomics and custom PCB layout are in progress.
caseStudy.nextSteps: Transition from perfboard to a custom two-layer PCB; design an adjustable 3D-printed wearable headband; evaluate adaptive baseline drift rejection.

flagships.title: Cellular Fingerprint Positioning System
flagships.subtitle: GPS-Denied Localization via RF Signal Fingerprints
flagships.description: My final-year Electrical Engineering capstone investigation at Adeleke University. Investigating position estimation algorithms in urban and indoor environments using cellular signal fingerprints (GSM/LTE RSSI, Cell ID, LAC) where satellite GPS signals are severely attenuated or unavailable.

caseStudy.problem: Satellite GPS signals suffer dramatic attenuation, multipath distortion, and power drain inside concrete buildings and high-density urban areas. Asset tracking and emergency location require an alternative positioning mechanism utilizing existing terrestrial cellular infrastructure.
caseStudy.difficulty: Cellular Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) exhibits high temporal and spatial variance caused by shadow fading, structural multipath, and dynamic network load balancing, rendering naive geometric trilateration error-prone.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Formulated the research methodology, assembled the hardware survey logging rig (microcontroller + cellular modem running AT commands), gathered empirical RSSI vectors across campus reference points, and implemented baseline fingerprint matching algorithms.

components.name: Base Station Array
components.desc: Multiple commercial cell towers (serving and neighbor cells) broadcasting GSM/LTE beacon channels.

components.name: Logging Test Rig
components.desc: Hardware transceiver interrogating modem registers (AT+CSQ, AT+CREG, AT+COPS) with timestamped coordinates.

components.name: Spatial Radio Map (Offline)
components.desc: Calibrated database associating reference locations (X, Y) with multi-dimensional RSSI fingerprint vectors.

components.name: Pattern Matching Engine (Online)
components.desc: K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and probabilistic matching determining estimated position from unknown vectors.

researchDetails.featuresLogged: Serving Cell ID (CID), Location Area Code (LAC), Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), and neighboring cell signal measurements.
researchDetails.algorithmExploration: Evaluating Euclidean k-NN vs Weighted k-NN and probabilistic modeling to handle signal fluctuation.
researchDetails.currentStage: Hardware logging rig calibrated; offline grid sampling actively ongoing across outdoor-to-indoor transition zones on campus at Adeleke University.
researchDetails.limitations: Accuracy is constrained by commercial base station density, indoor structural attenuation, and dynamic network rebalancing. Research is actively ongoing as part of degree requirements.

caseStudy.currentStatus: Survey rig functional. Initial grid measurements logged. Algorithm benchmarking and thesis evaluation in progress.
caseStudy.nextSteps: Complete full campus grid survey, evaluate Weighted k-NN against spatial interpolation models, and document empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) error curves.

flagships.title: Know Your Protocol (KYP)
flagships.subtitle: On-Chain Protocol Research & Accountability Platform
flagships.description: A protocol accountability platform built around economic commitments, wallet stakes, and verifiable on-chain follow-through. Users research protocols through an AI synthesis pipeline, lock stakes in smart contracts, and have their activity verified across EVM protocols without custom event signatures.

caseStudy.problem: Web3 researchers and protocol contributors routinely make commitments to test or research protocols, yet lack verifiable mechanisms for economic follow-through. Existing tools rely on centralized human attestations or rigid, protocol-specific smart contract hooks.
caseStudy.difficulty: Creating a protocol-agnostic verification system that inspects a user's on-chain activity across any EVM protocol without requiring custom event signatures or proprietary ABI decoders, while operating a zero-cost autonomous verification heartbeat.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Architected the complete system: Svelte 5 frontend, smart contract commitment logic with automatic stake verification and slashing, a protocol-agnostic on-chain event scanner using indexed getLogs, and a zero-cost heartbeat worker architecture.

components.name: AI Research Pipeline
components.desc: Dual-tier synthesis pipeline (Flash + Deep Researcher via Gemini) summarizing protocol parameters.

components.name: Solidity Commitment Vault
components.desc: Smart contracts locking stakes under a programmable 9-day, 3-strike accountability model.

components.name: Heartbeat Daemon
components.desc: Zero-cost heartbeat worker triggering periodic verification passes without paid subscription cron services.

components.name: Event Filter Engine
components.desc: Dynamic getLogs indexer scanning raw block logs for address interaction regardless of contract ABI.

tradeoffs: Protocol-agnostic log queries vs custom ABI decoders: chosen to allow users to verify engagement with any EVM smart contract on Monad without requiring pre-compiled contract artifacts.
Adaptive block-time estimation vs fixed timestamps: dynamically calculates inspection intervals from network block rate rather than hardcoded assumptions.
caseStudy.hardestBug: Eliminating RPC rate limits while scanning wide block ranges across multi-network environments (Monad Testnet and Mainnet). Solved by implementing exponential backoff with adaptive chunk size throttling in the custom getLogs worker.
caseStudy.currentStatus: Publicly deployed and verified on GitHub; recognized during the BuildAnything Spark Hackathon.
caseStudy.nextSteps: Add multi-sig commitment vaults and extend verification heuristics to cross-chain messaging events.

research.title: Cellular Signal Fingerprinting for GPS-Denied Localization
research.question: What positioning estimation accuracy can be achieved indoors using opportunistic GSM/LTE multi-cell RSSI vectors without dedicated anchor hardware?
research.motivation: Traditional satellite GPS signals degrade rapidly inside concrete buildings and industrial environments. Cellular fingerprinting leverages existing radio infrastructure by mapping unique multipath patterns.
research.methodology: Two-phase system: (1) An empirical offline survey collecting multi-cell RSSI, Cell ID, LAC, and Timing Advance across mapped test coordinates using AT-command modems. (2) An online positioning engine comparing real-time vectors via k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and probabilistic models.
research.status: Hardware survey rig operational. Initial grid sampling logged across transition zones on campus at Adeleke University. Benchmarking algorithms against measured radio data.
research.limitations: Accuracy is inherently sensitive to commercial base station topology, environmental multipath shifts, and human density changes.
research.nextSteps: Complete grid cross-validation, evaluate Weighted k-NN against spatial interpolation models, and document empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) positioning error curves for thesis presentation.

research.title: Low-Cost Biosignal Interfaces: Artifact Filtering on ESP32 Microcontrollers
research.question: How reliably can an entry-level dry-electrode EEG frontend be filtered in real time on an embedded dual-core microcontroller to detect deliberate trigger events without false positives?
research.motivation: Commercial brain-computer interfaces are prohibitively expensive for assistive care in developing nations. Integrating commercial-off-the-shelf ASICs like the NeuroSky TGAM with an ESP32 offers an ultra-low-cost pathway.
research.methodology: Configured 57,600-baud UART streaming with FreeRTOS task isolation; Core 0 handles checksum validation and 512Hz raw wave buffering; Core 1 runs dynamic thresholding to separate deliberate intentional blinks from ambient EMG jaw-clenching noise.
research.status: Benchtop test bench operational. Dual-core FreeRTOS firmware reliably decodes ThinkGear serial streams and executes threshold detection on test signals.
research.limitations: Does not decode continuous thoughts or sentences. Susceptible to movement artifacts without strict dry-electrode contact pressure.
research.nextSteps: Transition to a custom 2-layer PCB, fabricate an ergonomic 3D-printed adjustable headband, and incorporate active baseline drift filtering.

research.title: State Consistency & Reorg Recovery in High-Throughput EVM Networks
research.question: In sub-second block architectures with frequent micro-reorganizations, how can off-chain indexers maintain 100% deterministic state consistency without prohibitive multi-block finality lag?
research.motivation: High-throughput chains like Monad execute state rapidly, but asynchronous peer gossiping can cause temporary fork divergence that corrupts off-chain indexing databases if state is written immediately.
research.methodology: Implemented a triple-RPC quorum polling engine with a rolling FIFO block buffer. When parent-hash mismatch is detected across nodes, the indexer triggers an automated retroactive unwind, reversing mutated state up to the common ancestor before re-indexing.
research.status: Implemented and tested in MoyakiTraceEngine against concurrent RPC nodes under simulated network jitter.
research.limitations: Requires multi-RPC access and additional memory overhead for deep rolling buffers.
research.nextSteps: Extend the quorum engine with cryptographic state verification heuristics for cross-client consistency.

writing.title: Communicating in Functions
writing.summary: On engineering as communication — and why a function is just an idea precise enough to survive without its author. Examines interface boundaries, predictable contracts, and writing software that communicates intent clearly to both compilers and future teammates.

writing.title: Success Is 90% Luck and Informed Guessing
writing.summary: A probability framework for luck, consistency, and what to do when life hands you a defective die. Exploring Bayesian priors, increasing personal surface area for serendipity, and how technical builders turn probabilistic outcomes in their favor through relentless shipping.

narrative: I'm a final-year Electrical Engineering student at Adeleke University, Nigeria, and an independent builder working across software and physical systems.

My projects span real-time networking, blockchain infrastructure, AI agents, embedded electronics, and telecommunications. I enjoy taking unfamiliar technical problems apart, learning the underlying principles, and building systems I can test and improve.

I'm looking for an engineering team where I can contribute, learn from experienced technical peers, and work on challenging problems. I also intend to continue building independent projects and documenting my research.
